abstract: 69 (9.5%) of 724 patients with testicular cancer first seen at the Royal Marsden Hospital over the 10-year period 1975 to 1984 had a history of cryptorchidism. 11 patients had an uncorrected undescended testis when their testicular cancer was diagnosed, and 58 had had an orchidopexy or an orchidectomy for undescended testis. There are no general population data with which to compare the 15.9% (11/69) of testicular cancer patients with uncorrected cryptorchidism. However, the distribution of age at orchidopexy (or orchidectomy) of the 58 patients treated for undescended testis was almost identical to that expected on the basis of national rates. The age at treatment of undescended testis appears to have no effect on the risk of testicular cancer.
abstract_ja: 1975年から1984年の10年間にRoyal Marsden病院で初診された精巣がん患者724例のうち、69例(9.5%)に停留精巣の既往があった。精巣がん診断時に未矯正の停留精巣を有していた患者は11例であり、58例は停留精巣に対して精巣固定術または精巣摘除術を受けていた。停留精巣の治療を受けた58例の施行年齢の分布は、全国的な罹患率から予想される分布とほぼ同一であった。停留精巣に対する治療の年齢は精巣がんのリスクに影響を与えないようである。
